passage: Swati here. I sat next to Devang on Thursday before our seminar. He was glowing. "I can see it," he said, eyes shut. "The slides, the pause, everyone clapping, Yamini ma'am nodding." He had pictured it every night that week. He never opened his slides on another laptop and never checked the cable. When his turn came, the projector showed only a blue screen. He froze with the pen drive in his hand, said, "It worked yesterday," and stood there for a full minute. Yamini ma'am asked whether he could talk without slides. He shook his head. I don't know what was in his mind. He only looked like someone who had never once pictured this.

qa.q: What did the projector show when Devang's turn came?
qa.a: The projector showed only a blue screen.

qa.q: What might Devang have been feeling as he stood there after saying "It worked yesterday"?
qa.a: Devang was probably shocked and panicked, and perhaps embarrassed, since he froze for a full minute, though Swati cannot be sure.

qa.q: What could Devang have practised beforehand?
qa.a: Devang could have rehearsed a fallback, such as carrying a printed copy of the slides or practising the main points aloud without a screen.

qa.q: How might Yamini have felt when Devang shook his head?
qa.a: Yamini may have felt concerned for Devang, wanting to help but seeing the talk could not go on as planned.

grounding: Shows a student imagining only a perfect, applauded presentation and having no plan when the projector fails.

passage:
Sunday night. Mridul lay on his hostel bed and pictured Tuesday's presentation on water harvesting. He walks in. Slides flow. The professor nods. Classmates clap at the end. He replayed it three times and fell asleep smiling.
His roommate Yusuf asked on Monday, "Did you practise?"
"In my head. I'm ready."
"What if the projector acts up? It did in my class last week."
"It won't," Mridul said.
Tuesday. The projector showed a blue screen. The technician took ten minutes. Mridul stood at the front with no printout and no notes, trying to remember what was on slide four. He skipped half his points, lost the order, and finished early. The professor wrote something in her notebook without looking up.
That evening he told Yusuf, "I imagined everything except the part that went wrong."

qa.q: How long did the technician take?
How did Mridul feel standing at the front without slides?
qa.a: He felt panicked and lost, trying to remember slide four and skipping half his points.

qa.q: What would you change first in how Mridul prepared?
qa.a: Rehearse aloud at least once, and imagine the projector failing, then carry a printout or notes as a backup.

qa.q: How might Yusuf see what happened on Tuesday?
qa.a: Yusuf may feel sorry for Mridul but not surprised, since Yusuf had warned Mridul about the projector.

grounding: It shows a student picturing a perfect presentation and never rehearsing what to do if the projector fails, so the simulation made him feel ready without preparing him.

passage:
Arnab, you keep saying you've got the seminar "all in your head". Let your Ujjwal Chacha tell you about my final-year viva.
The night before, I lay in bed and played it like a film. I walk in, the examiners smile, my slides are beautiful, they ask easy questions, I answer brilliantly, they shake my hand. I watched that film maybe ten times. I felt completely ready.
I never once asked, what if something goes wrong?
Next morning, the power went off in the whole block. No projector. The examiners said, "Just explain it on the board."
I had never practised without slides. I couldn't remember the order of my own chapters. I drew one diagram wrong. I got a pass, but only just, and I walked out shaking.
That film in my head made me feel ready, beta. It just didn't make me ready.

qa.q: What did the examiners say when the power went off?
qa.a: The examiners said, "Just explain it on the board."

qa.q: How did Ujjwal feel walking out after the viva?
qa.a: Ujjwal felt shaken and embarrassed, having scraped a pass after feeling completely ready the night before.

qa.q: At the moment the power went off, what earlier choice could have saved Ujjwal, and why?
qa.a: Practising once without slides would have helped, because Ujjwal would have known his chapter order without the projector.

qa.q: How might the examiners have seen Ujjwal's viva?
qa.a: They may have seen a student who knew the topic but was badly thrown by a simple problem, which showed a lack of real preparation.

grounding: It shows a student who imagines only a perfect viva and never rehearses for a failure, so he feels ready without being prepared.
